question: Should every message-action entry point accept JSON-string `channelData`, reject malformed JSON, and drop the entire opaque payload when any protected runtime-context marker appears?
rationale: This decides both what provider-specific content becomes executable after normalization and whether existing malformed callers fail instead of having their metadata ignored; code and CI cannot establish the intended trust and compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve the strict shared contract
options.body: Accept valid object JSON at all covered boundaries, reject malformed or non-object input, and retain whole-field fail-closed suppression for protected context.

options.title: Preserve malformed-input compatibility
options.body: Parse valid object JSON but omit invalid `channelData` while allowing otherwise valid visible text to continue, with explicit compatibility tests.

options.title: Narrow the normalization boundary
options.body: Limit string parsing to the internal-source path until generic message-action callers are intentionally included in the public contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the strict shared contract
recommendation.body: Accept valid object JSON at all covered boundaries, reject malformed or non-object input, and retain whole-field fail-closed suppression for protected context.

likelyOwner.reason: The commit history shows the broadest ownership of the central outbound runner, source-reply routing, and adjacent message security policy.
